title: Service-fingerprint incident board and adaptive-error-taxonomy
creator: Marta Chen
description:
Summary:
Build a unified incident board that groups failures by deterministic service 'fingerprints' (request surface + route + model variant + client route) and presents an adaptive taxonomy-driven error surface. The board will drive both on-call triage and automated downstream rollups for dashboards and paging.

Goals:
- Provide a single-pane incident view that groups alerts by failure fingerprint instead of only by service or host.
- Surface failure taxonomy buckets (timeout, overload/backpressure, model_error, protocol_error, auth/perm, kv_cache_miss, data_validation) with mappings to HTTP/gRPC codes and runtime signals.
- Implement adaptive thresholds for alerting: thresholds slide based on request volume/p95 baseline per-fingerprint to reduce noisy pages during legitimate traffic shifts.
- Wire tracing hooks and log/metric enrichment so every failure has trace_id, fingerprint_key, model_version, gpu_pool, and route metadata.

Acceptance criteria:
1) New Grafana board (link below) shows grouped fingerprints with counts, p50/p95 latency, error_rate, and top contributing error kinds.
2) Each fingerprint card includes links to 5 most recent traces and the representative error signature.
3) Alerting uses adaptive thresholds (configurable per-project) and reduces noise vs. current static SLO alerts in a 30-day simulation.
4) Documentation + playbook in Confluence with example triage flows and mapping table to HTTP/gRPC codes.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Fingerprint key will be constructed from: model_id|route|input_shape_bucket|client_tier|handler_path. Trade-off: reduces cardinality but may hide micro-variants; will iterate if debugging needs higher cardinality.
- Adaptive thresholds will use percentile baselines (rolling 7d p95) with a floor/ceiling to avoid pathological baselines during low traffic. Introduces complexity in alerting logic; mitigated by conservative default config for first rollout.
- We will not attempt automated blame assignment to engineers in v1. That will be a follow-up once fingerprints are stable.

Telemetry changes (implementation notes):
- Tracing hooks: add fingerprint_key tag to root span in serving runtime and propagate to downstream services.
- Metrics: new metric names (dot-separated):
  - inference.fingerprint.requests{fingerprint_key} (counter)
  - inference.fingerprint.latency_ms.p50/p95{fingerprint_key} (histogram/summary)
  - inference.fingerprint.errors_total{fingerprint_key, error_kind}
  - inference.fingerprint.kv_cache_miss{fingerprint_key}
- Logs: structured log field "fingerprint_key" and "error_kind"; ensure sampling config preserves one trace/span per minute per-fingerprint.
- Pipeline: ingest metrics via existing metrics pipeline; add enrichment stage in log/Kafka pipeline to attach model_version and gpu_pool from meta-store using fingerprint_key cache.

Failure taxonomy mapping (initial):
- timeout: server-side deadline exceeded / grpc DEADLINE_EXCEEDED / HTTP 504. Root signals: p95 latency spike, kv cache miss, downstream datastore latency.
- overload: backpressure or queue rejects / HTTP 429 / grpc RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. Root signals: concurrent in-flight > capacity, queuing latency up, gpu queue length.
- model_error: invalid_model_output, nan/inf tokens, segmentation faults / process exit on worker. Map to internal error_kind 'model_error' + exit codes.
- protocol_error: malformed request, bad framing / HTTP 400 or grpc INVALID_ARGUMENT.
- auth/perm: unauthorized/forbidden / HTTP 401/403 or grpc UNAUTHENTICATED/ PERMISSION_DENIED.
- infra_oom: OOM or OOM-kill on host; correlate with node metrics.
- rate_limit: client quota exceeded / HTTP 429 but distinguish via rate_limit flag.
- data_validation: input validation failures before model invocation.

Mapping table (examples to include in Confluence):
- HTTP 504 -> timeout
- gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED -> timeout
- HTTP 429 + header 'x-rate-limit' -> rate_limit
- HTTP 502 with model stderr containing 'nan' -> model_error

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: schema + proto changes for trace tag, metric names approved; create enrichment service recipe. (OWNERS: infra-observability)
- Week 2: instrument runtime, add fingerprint generation, end-to-end trace tagging in staging. (OWNERS: serving-runtime)
- Week 3: metrics pipeline enrichment + Grafana dashboard prototype; link traces. (OWNERS: telemetry)
- Week 4: run 30-day synthetic noise simulation and calibrate adaptive thresholds; update alert rules. (OWNERS: SRE)

Open tasks / PRs / links:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7812 (fingerprint tags + span enrichment)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/489 (metric names + pipeline enrichment)
- Draft dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/observability/service-fingerprint-board
- Playbook: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/OBS/Service+Fingerprint+Incident+Board
- Design notes: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XFingerprintDesign/view

Progress log (high level):
- 2026-02-28: RFC approved in design review; decided on 5-field fingerprint key (Marta).
- 2026-03-03: Runtime prototype pushed, span tag added for root span (PR #7812). Diego opened telemetry PR for metric names.
- 2026-03-08: SRE provided feedback: require floor values for adaptive thresholds and opt-out per team. Added to spec.
- 2026-03-12: End-to-end traces observed in staging; sample volume adjustments required to keep collector costs bounded.
- 2026-03-14: Dashboard prototype live in internal Grafana; working on alert rule migration and simulation tests.

Review feedback and next steps:
- PM review (Anika Rao): ensure per-customer opt-out and link to Dedicated/Private routing logic.
- Design review (Talia Nguyen): add compact visualization for on-call; suggested colorblind-friendly palette.
- Engineering notes: need a migration plan for existing SLO alerts to avoid duplicate paging; plan to gradually switch routes to fingerprint-based alerts using feature flags.

Test plan:
- Unit tests: fingerprint generation deterministic across scale and different input shapes.
- Integration: end-to-end trace + metric pipeline test using synthetic replay harness.
- Load test: simulate 100k rps with spike patterns to validate adaptive thresholds and ensure reduced false positives.

Rollout plan:
1) Instrument a small set of non-critical routes (canary) and monitor false positive rate for 7 days.
2) Expand to all internal infra routes, enable adaptive alerts in read-only mode to compare pages.
3) Switch to active paging when simulation shows >=25% reduction in noisy pages and no missed sev1s for 48h.

Notes for on-call and postmortems:
- Include fingerprint_key in postmortem templates to improve root cause searches.
- If an uncommon fingerprint shows up with >5% of total errors across the fleet, mark it as candidate for model onboarding or routing change.
